parts.title: Read It or Make It? Which Mind Map Do You REMEMBER? (Part 1) | Study Skills P3–P6
parts.description:
Pip reads a ready-made mind map. Basil makes his own, from memory. Which one helps you remember more? Play the word puzzle test, find out why working something out makes it stick (scientists call it the generation effect), and spot the mistake when Momo "makes her own" map. A study-skills special for Primary 3 to 6 Science (Singapore), for kids aged 8 to 12, with Heart and the pet buddies Pip, Momo and Basil. Part 1 of 2.

In this part:
• Read it or make it?
• The word puzzle test
• Look closer: reading a map vs making one
• The memory test: the generation effect
• HOLD ON! Is copying the same as making?
• Memory first
• Spot the hidden crow!

Key words: make your own, generation effect, memory first.
Watch Part 2: make one together in TheOneApp, check and fix, and space it out: who remembers more one week later?

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

The science, short and honest: Scientists have tested these study habits many times: working something out yourself helps you remember it (the generation effect); drawing a map from memory and then checking it beats copying it (retrieval practice); and drawing it again after a few days beats reading it many times at once (spaced practice). One day, three days and a week is a simple plan; any spread-out days work.
Make your own mind map in TheOneApp: tap Mind Maps, then ✏️ Make my own mind map, pick your chapter and tap ＋ Start a new mind map. When you are done, tap ✅ Mark my mind map. https://theoneapp-ten.vercel.app
Safety and care: We look at crows and community cats, and we do not feed, chase or touch them.

parts.title: One Week, One Blank Page. Who Remembers MORE? (Part 2) | Make Your Own Mind Map
parts.description:

Make a mind map with us in TheOneApp, step by step (Mind Maps · Make my own mind map · Start a new mind map · Mark my mind map · Compare with the poster), spot the mistake on Pip's poster, and be an idea in a picture of Basil's memory. Part 2 of 2 of a study-skills special for Primary 3 to 6 Science (Singapore), kids aged 8 to 12.
